$comment: Where the application is designed to send data, and the most it may send to each place.
Read by scripts/security-scan-egress.mjs on every push to main. A destination or server
endpoint with no entry here is reported the moment code first references it, and a position
sent to a destination whose mayReceive has no position class fails the check outright.
The LLM review applies the same contracts to what a regex cannot see (request bodies).
mayReceive uses a fixed vocabulary, least to most revealing: none, time, coarse-area,
precise-position, identifier, user-text, user-file, user-audio, usage-stats, audit-metadata,
video-frame, menu-summary, session-data. See scripts/security-scan-egress.mjs for the definitions and
docs/UserDataEgressCheck.md for how to add an entry. Add one only with an honest statement
of what the destination receives; the entry is the public contract.

server-internal audit writer, not a browser API. Retains UTC time, random request ID, server/script/method, transport-peer address, original/effective numeric account IDs, fixed event/outcome/reason/status and SHA-256 resource/subject identifiers in the site's PHP error logger (container error stream by default) or local AUTHPRIV syslog. Hashes are correlatable and guessable for low-entropy inputs, not anonymous. No raw filenames, share URLs, coordinates, request bodies or credentials are retained. No application network destination is accepted. This contract covers those local sinks only: any downstream collector, including configured PHP or system-log forwarding, needs a separate site review naming its concrete destination, the same or a smaller field set, reader roles and retention before forwarding is enabled; this is not a wildcard approval for remote collectors.
serverEndpoints.trigger: authentication outcomes and attempted/completed instrumented API requests, including reads and refusals, automatically when AUTH_MODE=cert or when the operator explicitly enables AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED in another mode; otherwise disabled. No per-request user action is required for these security records.
